### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f93d95ad1640c3bb40ed53700316611b710913da` — the merge of head `40182cb5ffc8b95957e96def6a7e55a8460c9a55` into base `4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f93d95ad1640c3bb40ed53700316611b710913da && git checkout f93d95ad1640c3bb40ed53700316611b710913da
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc 40182cb5ffc8b95957e96def6a7e55a8460c9a55 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc && git merge --no-ff 40182cb5ffc8b95957e96def6a7e55a8460c9a55

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b71a82b76531059ad45ba224899aaadaa219ebc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `74983ea388b27ece483f9112df1b5c21e6efa1bd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, .changeset/29855-layers-draft-layer.md, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, packages/spec/src/api/meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts (read for the pins), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts (ledger depth), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`createMetaLayeredAnswer`, `META_ITEM_LAYERS`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`serveMetaItemLayered`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (layered dispatch), AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3 — all read in the live tree, none reviewed. The lane remainder at `TIER_DEFAULT` is the test file, the changeset prose and the regenerated mdx.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `GetMetaItemLayeredResponseSchema` gains `draft: z.unknown().optional()` — a widening of a published response accept set (`packages/spec/src/api/**`, exported). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is **right**. The type `GetMetaItemLayeredResponse` gains an optional key; no existing member changes; an answer without the key still parses (pinned). Correct.
2. `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema.packageId` — describe text only, no accept-set change. Correct.
3. `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains the row `api/GetMetaItemLayeredResponse:draft`. The ledger is built from `schema.properties` ONE LEVEL DEEP (`build-schemas.ts` L107–117 and `nested-authorable-keys.test.ts` say so in as many words: recursing would publish 14,376 nested keys), and `GetMetaItemLayeredResponse` is a ledgered schema, so a new TOP-LEVEL member moves the shard. The regenerated row is correct and the only one the member can move. This row is what ② turns on.
4. `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`: two rows regenerated. I compared both cells against the describes in the head tree: the `draft` row and the layered-request `packageId` row match the Zod text byte for byte. Correct.
5. No export added, so `api-surface/`, `export-origins` and the declaration map do not move — consistent with the file list. Correct.
6. `check:test-typecheck` ledger unchanged — the one new compile-time pin is in a `tsconfig.test.json` file, no new error. Plausible from the diff; CI's Type Check lanes did not conclude on this head (see ②).

### ② Semver level

**Must-fix — the head's own `Check Changeset` is red, and the gate is right.** Run 41604712591 job 125811566989, step `check-changeset-no-major --base`, verdict `none-baseline-moved`: "This PR declares clause-② `yes (widening)` and metadata-protocol `none`, and it moves a metadata-protocol baseline the ratchets record: packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json". The changeset at this head grades `@objectstack/spec` `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body as read by that run said the same.

Which is right. Ruling A as mechanised (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` L907–945): the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` line alone, and "where the existing ratchets can SEE a protocol change, a declared `none` over it is refused: a changed `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` shard is a key added or removed." The gate's remedy text is explicit that the fix is the declaration, never the baseline: "a baseline is never edited to quiet this gate." AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3 says the same in prose ("a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`"). So on this diff the right declaration is `Metadata-protocol: added` with `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, in both carriers (the gate reads the body line from `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, L1845; `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the changeset).

Why the precedent did not transfer. PR #29779 (`f87239ae7b`) added `data.noticeCode` to `CloneFlowResponseSchema` — a key NESTED under `data`. The ledger records `api/CloneFlowResponse:data` and nothing beneath it (one level deep, above), so that shard did not move, `none` was invisible to the ratchet, and `patch` passed. Here `draft` is a top-level member of a ledgered schema, the shard moved, and the ratchet saw it. The card's "precedent PR #29779 ⇒ `patch`" was a reading of the gate's blind spot, not of its rule. Semver-wise `minor` is also the honest level for a new optional response member.

One observation, not this PR's to fix: under this gate the level of two equally additive REST-response members depends on nesting depth (top-level ⇒ `minor`, nested ⇒ `patch`), and `api/*` response schemas are in a ledger whose rule text speaks of "what a metadata author can write". If a lane disagrees with REST response keys driving the level, that is a card against the ledger or the gate text, not a reason to keep `none` here.

Clause-②: line — `yes (widening)` matches the diff. Metadata-protocol: line — `none` is wrong at this head; `added` is right.

Check-runs on this head, read from the API: `Check Changeset` **failure** (real, above). Green: Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, filter, Flag docs. Not concluded: Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI, Build Core, Live E2E UI, Build Docs, every Type Check and Lint lane were **cancelled** when the branch moved to a newer head; the aggregators `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test UI` report `failure` only because their lanes concluded `cancelled` ("lane `typecheck-workspace` concluded `cancelled` -- expected `success`"), which is a cancellation signature, not a gate red. The `Check Changeset` red is this PR's own declaration, not a merge-base signature, so no exception applies. "All checks green" is not met on this head.

Head movement. The branch now carries one further commit after this head, which rewrites the changeset to `'@objectstack/spec': minor` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, and the live PR body now reads `Metadata-protocol: added`. That commit is a fix-only commit answering this finding; it is NOT reviewed by this record and owes a delta review by the same reviewer on its own head (contract-review.md: 只落发现的 commit 由同一复核者 delta 复核). Auto-merge is not armed; the PR is a draft; nothing to disarm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag (PR body, os-dev-report): `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema.packageId`'s describe now says it also scopes "the `draft` layer to that package's pending draft row". **Fine.** In scope: same `hits` file, and the card's Wanted names the draft "for the item (and the requested `packageId`, when given)". Accurate as the conditional it states: the producer already resolves draft rows by package (`findServedOverlayRow({ state: 'draft', packageId })` in `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` L266–270), so "when given, that package's draft row" is implementable without a decision. It says nothing about the absent case, which is exactly what the acceptance note defers to #29814 — consistent, not premature. (Pre-existing and not this PR's: the sentence says `packageId` scopes `code`, while on `main` it also addresses the overlay row via `contentPackageId`, L278.)
- Acceptance note "what a server does when `packageId` is absent is #29814's" — accepted, and escalated to #29814 with the existing addresses to report against: the protocol's `strictDraftReadAddress` (the draft the `version` names; `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` L203–214) and, at the transport, step 1c of `createMetaLayeredAnswer` (a name several packages hold, read naming none, is refused 409 before any layer is served).
- Escalated to #29814 (not a finding against the schema): (a) `createMetaLayeredAnswer` judges absence (step 1, 404) over `META_ITEM_LAYERS = ['effective','code','overlay']` and masks over `META_ITEM_MASKED_LAYERS`; the server half must decide whether `draft` joins the presence test (a draft-only item with no published layers) and must add it to the gate and mask lists ("⛔ A step is added there, never here"). (b) With `packageId` absent and "no injected columns", the body carries no package binding; the server half may want to report which package's draft row was served (as `overlayScope` does for `overlay`). Both are the consumer's to settle and report.
- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, judged against the #5882 ruling it cites, the card's Wanted, and its first consumer #29814 (the REST route `serveMetaItemLayered`, the runtime dispatcher, and the shared chain `createMetaLayeredAnswer`):

- **Shape — a `/layers` member, not a `?state=draft` switch: holds.** #5882 B retired "two shapes, chosen by query flag" so one path has one response shape; a switch that changes the plain read's representation is that pattern. `/layers` is already the untranslated, stored-at-each-layer view (REST `serveMetaItemLayered`: "Not translated and not cached, both deliberately"). The new docblock paragraph states this accurately; the #5882 rationale paragraph is byte-identical to `main` save "three-layer" → "layered", which the fourth layer makes true.
- **Name `draft`: fine.** The three existing layers are named by what they are, not by row state, so `draft` is the first state-named layer; but it is the stored draft overlay and nothing else, the card proposed it, triage endorsed it under the veto window, and the Studio/Setup buffer code already spells `draft ?? …`. No better name is owed.
- **`z.unknown().optional()`: holds.** Same carrier as `code`/`overlay`/`effective` (`z.unknown()`, which accepts `null`), so the three-way state is absent / `null` / object. The three runtime pins cover all three and the ablation shows the object and `null` pins are load-bearing. The compile-time pin `LayeredDeclaresDraft` keeps the consumer cast-free.
- **"absent = not served, never no draft": consistent and necessary.** Until #29814 lands every server answers without the key; a consumer that read absence as "no draft" would fall through to `overlay ?? code` and silently lose the author's draft — the very defect of #29814. The sentence follows the `_diagnostics` precedent in the same schema ("absence means no opinion, never valid") and the #29779 `noticeCode` one. The corollary the describe implies — a server that serves the layer always emits the key, `null` when nothing is pending — is what #29814 must pin.
- **"untranslated, ungoverned, with no injected columns": accurate and implementable.** On `main` the layered producer builds `overlay` as `convertStoredItem(type, storedRowDocument(rec))` with no `governServedObject` (that is applied to `effective` only, L506), and the REST/runtime chain does not translate it. The `?state=draft` item read, by contrast, goes through `serveItem` → `decorateMetadataItem` and `serveDraft` (`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` L105–130), which is the governed, decorated copy the card measured. A draft row served through the same `convertStoredItem(storedRowDocument(row))` path is exactly what the describe promises. "Exactly as stored" reads as `code`'s "exactly as shipped" does: the transport's per-caller gate (#20156, whole for whoever may write the item) and the ADR-0106 mask apply to every layer alike, and that is the chain's documented contract, not this describe's to restate.
- **`null` when no draft is pending: holds.** Parallel to `overlay: null` ("not customised") and distinct from the strict `?state=draft` read's 404 `no_draft`, which is the right split: `/layers` reports, it does not refuse.
- **`packageId` scoping: holds** (③ above).

No must-fix in ④. No should-fix in ④. The one must-fix in this record is ②'s declaration/level, which the gate itself names.

Lane remainder (not reviewed here, noted for the ACCEPT): `meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts` L76, the `LayeredCarriesNoItem` alias, lost the space between `=` and `Assert` — cosmetic; `Lint · ESLint` did not conclude on this head.

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40182cb5ffc8b95957e96def6a7e55a8460c9a55`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + .changeset/29855-layers-draft-layer.md (the one file the delta commit moves), the live PR body (both declaration lines and the level bullet), the two `Check Changeset` runs on this head, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (read), and the prior record on `74983ea388b27ece483f9112df1b5c21e6efa1bd`, comment 6599317618, whose ①, ③ and ④ this delta carries forward unchanged.

Delta review: the same reviewer, on the one fix-only commit after the FAIL head. The compare `74983ea388…40182cb5ff` holds one commit and one file, `.changeset/29855-layers-draft-layer.md`, +2 −2: `'@objectstack/spec': patch` → `minor`, `Metadata-protocol: none` → `added`. No `hits` file moved, so ④ is the prior record's and is not re-rendered; the tier stays `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because the PR's committed tree still carries the published schema.

### ① Derived judgments

Unchanged from 6599317618 ①: the diff against `main` publishes the same accept-set widening (`GetMetaItemLayeredResponseSchema.draft`, optional), the same ledger row `api/GetMetaItemLayeredResponse:draft`, the same two regenerated mdx rows, no export. The delta commit publishes nothing new; it changes what the release ledger says about the same diff.

### ② Semver level

**The must-fix of 6599317618 is answered.** At this head the changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` `minor` and declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: added`; the live PR body carries the same two lines (lines 4–5) and its "What changes" bullet now reads "`@objectstack/spec` minor, with both declaration lines", so body, changeset and diff agree. `added` is the kind the moved `authorable-surface` shard records (a key entered), `minor` is the level ruling A assigns it, and the pair is the shape `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` both accept for a non-breaking widening (no `(narrowing)` arm, no `!`, no banner owed).

Gate verdicts on this head, read from the check-runs API:
- `Check Changeset` ran twice. Run 125813870035 is `failure` with the prior head's signature (`none-baseline-moved`: body line read as `Metadata-protocol: none`) — it fired on the push, before the PR body was edited, and the gate reads the declaration from the event's body. Run 125814393589 is `success`: "LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `yes (widening)` and metadata-protocol `added`, and no package whose published source it moves is graded `patch`." The gate re-reads the body on the `edited` event by design, so the newest run of this check on this head governs; the earlier red is superseded, not a standing red.
- Completed green: 23 (among them Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links). Skipped: 10 (opt-in and conditional workflows).
- Still `in_progress` at the time of this read: 31 — Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Build Core, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace, Lint · CI, release & engine gates. None has concluded red. The landing pre-check "every PR check green" is therefore not yet satisfiable from this read; the dispatching seat confirms it when these conclude. Nothing in the delta can move them: the one changed file is a changeset, which none of those lanes compile or test.

Clause-②: `yes (widening)` — right. Metadata-protocol: `added` — right at this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No new dev flag and no `open_questions` on the delta. The prior record's ③ stands: the request-side `packageId` describe edit is fine; the absent-`packageId` case, the `META_ITEM_LAYERS` / mask-list presence question and the draft row's package binding are escalated to #29814, the consumer, to settle and report.
- The PR body's level bullet was edited to match (`minor`); the body's Human Minimum §5 tick ("both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset") is now true.
- PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note owed. PR is a draft; auto-merge not armed; nothing to disarm.
- Observation carried from 6599317618, not this PR's: the ledger's one-level depth makes the level of an additive REST-response member depend on nesting (top-level ⇒ `minor`, nested ⇒ `patch`); a card against the gate or ledger text if a lane disagrees.

### ④ Design judgment

Not re-rendered: the delta moves no `hits` file. The judgment on `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` in 6599317618 ④ stands in full — the `/layers` member over a `?state=draft` switch holds against #5882 B; the `draft` name, the `z.unknown().optional()` tri-state, the "untranslated, ungoverned, no injected columns" describe and its `packageId` scoping are accurate and implementable against the layered producer and the REST/runtime chain; the regenerated mdx matches the describe byte for byte. No must-fix, no should-fix. Lane remainder note (cosmetic `=`/`Assert` spacing in the test file) is unchanged and is the lane seat's.
